, in the context of the current study, the results obtained from the analysis of the 5' UTR of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, as well as the results obtained from analysis of the 3'UTR of the virus (see the previous study by the same group), are consistent with a leader primed mechanism of transcription of SARS-CoV2.
the mechanism of transcription initiation in the coronaviruses is leader priming.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the leader RNA in coronavirus-infected host cells can serve as a template to generate leader-related small RNAS, which can then be used to prime the transcription of the viral genome.
the leader RNA of the virus is transcribed in the cell, and this leader RNA is then processed by the Dicer enzyme to form the small RNA.
the leader RNA is not just a transcriptional promoter, but a functional RNA in itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5′-end of a coronavirus transcript does not have to be capped to be recognized as an RNA polymerase primer.

leader-related small RNs in coronavirus-infected mammalian cells are derived from leader-primed transcription, and that leader priming is a common mechanism for the production of leader-derived small RNAs in both mammalian and insect cells infected with coronavirus.
the leader is the template for all of the subgenomic mRNA transcription in coronavirus-infected host cells.
